title: Field inside aluminium at 100 MHz
caption: In a conductor the field decays as e^{−z/δ}. For aluminium (σ = 3.5 × 10⁷ S m⁻¹) at 100 MHz, δ = √(2/ωμσ) = 8.5 μm. After one skin depth the amplitude is 1/e = 0.37; household foil (about 16 μm) is about 1.9 skin depths thick and leaves only 0.15 of the amplitude, so it attenuates strongly.
alt: Graph of field amplitude relative to the surface against depth in aluminium from 0 to 30 micrometres: an exponential decay through 0.37 at 8.5 micrometres and 0.15 at 16 micrometres.
description: The horizontal axis is the depth into the metal in micrometres; the vertical axis is the field amplitude relative to its value at the surface.
The curve is e^{−z/δ} with δ = 8.5 μm, the skin depth of aluminium at 100 MHz.
At z = δ the amplitude is 1/e = 0.37.
At 16 μm, the thickness of foil, it is 0.15.
